title: Staking a spot early for Red, White & BOOM! - NewsBreak
text: COLUMBUS, Ohio ( WCMH ) – Every year, more than 400,000 people flock to downtown Columbus for Red, White & BOOM! , and as always, people made sure to claim their spots early. By Thursday morning, Downtown Columbus is going to be filled with people. For many, this is a long-time family tradition that allows people to hang out, eat some good food, and talk with the people set up next to them before the extravagant fireworks show begins. “I’ve been coming to the BOOM, probably, 40-something years,” resident Carl Roddy said. “My mom and dad, they had eight of us come down. That was the event to them, you know. And we spent the night back in the days, 40-something years ago.” Roddy comes from a large family, and he’s been attending Red, White, and BOOM! since the beginning. It’s a tradition they make sure lives on every year. “It’s a lot of grandkids, trying to get them to get out the house and get away from that game and show them the traditions that we love to do,” Roddy said. “The picnic. The family coming out from out of town.” Roddy wasn’t the only one claiming a spot early on Wednesday. Throughout the lawns Downtown, visitors will see chairs and caution tape, meaning that spot is reserved. “I have six kids and I have 12 grandkids, so I try to get the best spot for how many kids are coming,” resident Kim Starr said. Every year, Starr claims her spot the day before BOOM!. “My reunion is this, you know, I try to get everybody together and we play cards and we play games and play football and basketball and all the things that kids bring down balls,” she said. Red, White and BOOM! may be a reunion for many families, but it’s also a time to meet new people you otherwise would have never met. That goes for Starr and Chris Howard. For years now, the two have been claiming their spots near one another. Over the years, they’ve become good friends, looking out for one another. “You meet them every year, you know?” Howard said. “They’re going to be there and as soon as you see, you say ‘Hey, how are you doing?’ She (Starr) gave me a hug when I came, and so that’s that you build relationships that last for a long time.” “We just have such fun talking, you know, talk about our life and stories that we have to tell and learn about each other and that’s just so much fun,” Starr said. Many are excited for the show tomorrow and plan to spend most of the day taking in the Downtown festivities. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to NBC4 WCMH-TV.
